Team — forwarding Anya's clarifications. Draft replies below; please correct and attach the artifacts referenced. Timeline: bundle and share to Anya by EOD Monday (EU time).

Inline answers to the security questions (draft):

1) Logs: Our ingestion pipeline for customer logs for EU tenants remains within EU Central. We do not route raw customer logs to non-EU analytics clusters. Aggregate telemetry (non-identifiable usage metrics) may cross-region for platform analytics, but raw request/response traces and access logs remain in EU Central until deleted per retention policy. (Ben: please attach network capture and storage ACL snapshot proving EU S3 buckets + ACL timestamps.)

2) Backups: Automated daily snapshots for tenant state and objects are retained in EU Central. We maintain an optional cross-region replication policy for disaster recovery which is disabled by default for production tenants unless customers opt in via written agreement. (Irene: we need the snapshot retention manifest and replication flag screenshot.)

3) Keys: Customer KMS keys for Medtria can be provisioned in EU and we will use HSM-backed key material stored on EU-resident HSMs (partner HSM provider: EuroHSM). Keys are tenant-scoped and not exported outside the region. (Sean: please attach the KMS partitioning diagram and EuroHSM attestation reference.)

4) Fallback paragraph (for SLA appendix — please refine):

"In the event of temporary capacity constraints in EU Central that would materially impact Medtria's service availability, Redwood will by default attempt to scale within the reserved EU capacity and activate standby nodes located in adjacent EU zones. If no EU capacity is available and Medtria has provided prior written consent, Redwood may temporarily route customer requests to an alternative region for the shortest possible duration necessary to maintain service continuity. Any such cross-region routing will be preceded by notice to Medtria's security and procurement contacts when feasible, and Redwood will provide a post-incident report detailing duration, scope, and mitigation steps. Cross-region failover will not be used for archival or backup retention without explicit written permission from Medtria."

Deliverables to assemble: redwood_region_commitment_draft.pdf, redwood-eu-network-topology-v1.svg, privatelink-onboard-checklist.xlsx, redwood-caik-sig-slice-2027.pdf, redwood-soc2-excerpt-redacted.pdf, redwood-kms-partitioning-2027.pdf

If that looks OK I'll send the packet to Anya with the attachments and Drive folder.

Thanks — Marissa

Anya —

Thanks for the clarifying questions. Attached is the consolidated evidence packet and a short SLA appendix paragraph for your auditors. Quick answers to your items are inline below and the attachments are linked in the Drive folder.

Short answers (for quick paste):

1) Logs: Raw customer logs (request/response traces and access logs) for EU tenants are retained and processed solely within EU Central. We do not route raw customer logs to non-EU analytics clusters. Only anonymized, aggregate platform telemetry (no customer identifiers) may be used outside the region.

2) Backups and snapshots: Automated backups are retained in EU Central. Cross-region replication is available only by explicit customer opt-in and is disabled by default.

3) Keys: Customer keys for Medtria will be provisioned in the EU and stored in EuroHSM-backed HSMs in-region. Keys are tenant-scoped and not exportable; rotation and access logs are provided as part of the evidence pack.

4) Fallback (SLA appendix paragraph):

"In the event of temporary capacity constraints in EU Central that would materially impact Medtria's service availability, Redwood will first attempt to scale within EU capacity and activate standby nodes in adjacent EU zones. If no EU capacity is available and Medtria has provided prior written consent, Redwood may temporarily route customer traffic to an alternative region for the minimal duration required to preserve availability. Redwood will notify Medtria when feasible and deliver a post-incident report. Cross-region failover will not be used for archival or backup retention without explicit written permission from Medtria."
